---
title: "Check the playbook applies"
description: "Check the playbook applies, and how to treat your kind of work."
---

The playbook applies if both of these are true:

1. You collected, manipulated or interpreted data to answer a question.
2. Somebody is going to act on the answer.

This includes any [analytical output](../09-resources/r1-glossary.qmd) used internally, supplied to a sponsor or published externally.

If it applies, start at [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd).

## Find your kind of work

[Decide your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) for your own work. The second column is an example, not your score.

| The work | Example impact, or how to treat it | What else applies |
|------------------------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Exploratory analysis, an internal data investigation | Impact 1 | A colleague in your team still checks the headline numbers |
| A monthly operational dashboard, team workforce planning | Impact 2 | Score it once, at design. [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd) says when it is reviewed |
| An official statistics publication, such as Dental Statistics | Impact 3 | Ask the Lead Official for Statistics ([who to ask](../09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd)). The [Code of Practice for Statistics](../09-resources/r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd#the-code-of-practice-for-statistics) applies |
| A Freedom of Information (FOI) response, or a Parliamentary Question | Impact 3 | Score visibility only under [public visibility and reach](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/score-the-impact.qmd) |
| A Board report or a ministerial briefing | Impact 3 | [Visibility alone is not Level 4](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/score-the-impact.qmd#what-does-not-by-itself-justify-level-4) |
| A funding allocation formula, an eligibility model, a payment methodology, a major policy appraisal | Impact 4, so Level 4 BCA | Follow [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd) from scoping |
| A dataset supplied to a sponsor or a partner | Score it like any other analysis | The playbook applies when you supply it, not only when you publish it |
| A forecasting model informing budgets | Score it, then place it among the [eight model types](after-you-have-your-level.qmd#the-eight-types-of-analytical-model) | State the [uncertainty](../09-resources/r10-uncertainty.qmd) in the forecast |
| An algorithmic or machine learning tool that affects decisions about people | Score it, and separately check transparency scope | Check [transparency scope](../09-resources/r12-algorithmic-transparency-and-ai.qmd) at scoping |
| An AI assistant helping you write code, summarise or draft | You are still accountable for the work | Follow the five rules in [using AI tools to do the analysis](../09-resources/r12-algorithmic-transparency-and-ai.qmd#using-ai-tools-to-do-the-analysis) |
| Analysis you are reusing for a new purpose, or a one-off that has become a monthly production run | Check whether the original level still holds | Run [the four checks before reuse](../05-review/index.qmd#check-four-things-before-any-reuse). A one-off that becomes a production run is scored again |
| A published figure that has turned out to be wrong | Not a new piece of analysis | Follow [correcting a published figure](../09-resources/r6-when-something-is-wrong.qmd) |
| Work where there is not enough time for the assurance the level asks for | The level does not change | Follow [when time is short](after-you-have-your-level.qmd#when-there-is-not-enough-time) |

: Kinds of work, how each is treated, and what else applies to it
